Correct across the jaw gap, not farther along the approach: holder is to the right in the wrist image. Shift both world x and y slightly positive while maintaining clearance.
Holder is now between the jaws in the wrist view. Close and perform a short upward/backward retention test, keeping the grasp command fully closed.

Stop rotating near the elbow limit. Lower the open gripper at its current oblique downward angle to regain configuration margin and approach the fallen holder.

Lower in small increments to restore elbow margin and continue a short wrist-guided lateral correction. Keep the jaws open and avoid further rotation near the joint limit.
The far approach reached a joint limit and still missed the holder. Retract toward the robot and turn the gripper toward a frontal recovery approach while preserving joint continuity.
The rejected action moved nothing. Use millimeter-scale translation only to back away from the near-singular configuration before attempting any rotation.
Back out a little of the downward pitch rather than increasing it; use very small increments to leave the joint-limit region.
Reduce the rejected adjustment again and add a slight outward retreat, keeping the arm on its current branch.
Approach the fallen holder from a shallower angle to preserve joint margin, using the head view to shift the jaw center forward.
The forward approach is at the joint limit. Withdraw toward the robot and upward without rotating, then reorient to approach the holder from the near side.
Reorient the right gripper to reach from the near side, while retracting to a comfortable elbow-up pose rather than extending farther forward.
Complete the near-side grasp orientation above the fallen holder, with the open jaw gap across its width and a slow descent.
With the near-side configuration established, advance and lower toward the holder body while correcting rightward in the wrist image.
Continue the near-side approach lower and forward. The holder is still ahead of the fingertips; keep the open gap aligned before closing.
Correct the lateral jaw alignment to the right without pushing farther forward. Raise slightly to clear the tabletop during this correction.

The jaws closed below the holder corner rather than around its body. Reopen and raise the grasp center while advancing a short distance.
Close at the corrected holder-body height and test retention with a short upward and backward lift.
The grasp was empty. Reopen and advance the jaws farther around the holder end, making the approach shallower while compensating height.
The holder end now overlaps the open jaw region. Close fully, pause, and test retention with a short lift back toward reachable workspace.
The holder stayed on the table. Advance the open jaws deeper past its near corner at a slightly lower height before closing again.
Close the centered jaws at this deeper approach and test retention by retracting and lifting a short distance, keeping the command fully closed.

Finish closing and perform a slow upward/backward retention test while maintaining zero opening.

Align the jaw center with the nearer holder end rather than its far-side silhouette, then close and make a very small retention test.

Turn the open grasp toward the holder's near end while backing off slightly to preserve shoulder margin. Lower gradually to surround the body rather than close above it.
The entire holder is still ahead of the jaw contact region. Back off and descend to its actual fallen-body height before a deeper entry, keeping the elbow-up branch.

Advance farther with a compensating rise to retain shoulder margin; keep the open jaws centered on the near holder end.
Stop advancing at the continuity boundary. Close at the observed higher pose, then pull backward with a small lift to test whether the holder body is captured.

Change to a nearly horizontal entry and shift toward the holder body, rather than repeating the empty near-corner closure. Keep the jaws open during reorientation.

Correct the remaining offset across the jaw gap, then enter a short distance along the holder axis and close at fixed height. Stop if the continuity guard limits the entry.
